newsitem.title: USA: Ecuador digs in heels in Texaco enviro case.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador digs in heels in Texaco enviro case.

text.p: Ecuador is digging in its heels in a long-standing environmental lawsuit against Texaco Inc despite a string of disappointments in the U.S. courts.

In a press conference in New York on Wednesday, Ecuadoran Attorney General Leonidas Plaza Verduga reiterated his government's support for indigenous residents of the Amazon region who are suing Texaco for alleged environmental damage during the company's operations there from 1964 to 1992.
Plaza denounced Texaco for "irrational exploitation," asserting that the U.S. oil company "took no precautions at all and was only looking at the profit factor."
Plaza plans to meet with U.S. Justice Department officials in Washington on Friday to discuss this case and other bilateral issues.
Texaco rejects the charges, asserting that it complied with prevailing international environmental practices during its 28-year tenure.

"I find it surprising that, in a complete reversal of the Republic of Ecuador's previous position, the attorney general now seeks to intervene not as a defendant, but as a plaintiff," a Texaco spokesman said.
State-owned Petroecuador was the majority partner in Texaco's local operations, although the plaintiffs' attorneys say that Texaco made all the decisions.
Last November, U.S. District Court Judge Jed Rakoff dismissed the suit, asserting that the United States was not the appropriate forum for the case.
The Ecuadoran government and state-owned oil company Petroecuador subsequently intervened in support of the plaintiffs.
The plaintiffs then filed a motion asking Rakoff to reconsider his earlier ruling based on the intervention. The plaintiffs' attorneys say a decision on the motion is imminent.
The plaintiffs' attorneys argue that key decisions on Texaco's Ecuadoran operations were made at the company's headquarters in White Plains, New York, not in Quito.
The case was initially filed on November 3, 1993.
--P. Garip-Bertuol and T. Ashby New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
